itms-91064.title: ITMS-91064 Invalid Binary: NSPrivacyTracking fix
itms-91064.desc: An iOS build was rejected with ITMS-91064: NSPrivacyTracking was true while NSPrivacyTrackingDomains was empty. How it was fixed, and what is not verified.

review-info-needed.title: App Store Guideline 2.1 Information Needed: 6 items
review-info-needed.desc: My first App Store submission got a request for more information (Guideline 2.1), not a rejection. The six things Apple asked for and how they connect to earlier fixes.

xcode152-sdk.title: Firebase 12 on Xcode 15.2: why I pinned 11.4.0
xcode152-sdk.desc: On an old Mac stuck on Xcode 15.2, newer Firebase and AdMob SDKs fail to build. Which versions break, which I pinned (Firebase 11.4.0, AdMob 11.5.0), and why.

torecadash-watchdog.title: iOS app killed by watchdog 0x8BADF00D: SwiftUI fix
torecadash-watchdog.desc: An iOS app was force-quit by the watchdog (0x8BADF00D). A SwiftUI computed property re-filtered and re-sorted 951 articles on the main thread every body evaluation.

u2028.title: Python splitlines() breaks JSONL: U+2028 culprit
u2028.desc: Python splitlines() broke a JSONL file because 2 of 7,247 records contained U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR). Why it happens and the one-line fix: split on the newline only.

torecadash-ci.title: No TestFlight builds: Xcode Cloud 25 free hours
torecadash-ci.desc: New builds stopped appearing in TestFlight. My first diagnosis (“[ci skip] is blocking builds”) was wrong; the workflow built the iOS app on every commit.

apple-signin.title: Firebase Auth creates anonymous accounts on relaunch
apple-signin.desc: Force-quitting the app made Firebase create a new anonymous account each launch: 17 of 19 users were throwaway. Cause: reading currentUser too early.

logo-pop.title: Canvas 2x too large on Retina: inset:0 won’t stretch
logo-pop.desc: Burst particles appeared in the wrong place on high-DPI screens. A canvas with only inset:0 keeps its pixel size, so it was 2x larger in CSS on Retina.

crazygames.title: Rejected by CrazyGames with no reason: 4 causes
crazygames.desc: A game portal rejected my game with only “overall quality below expectations.” I recorded what the reviewer saw, found four causes and fixed them by measuring.

adgap.title: Ad interval by time, not by plays
adgap.desc: Why I replaced “one ad every 5 plays” with “7 minutes since the last ad” in a browser game, how it behaves, and what I still do not know.

ascii-text.title: Garbled Japanese in CrazyGames preview: ASCII fix
ascii-text.desc: One character broke in a game portal’s preview though the file bytes were correct. How I made the game immune without finding the cause.

deploy-gotchas.title: Works locally, breaks deployed: 4 static-site bugs
deploy-gotchas.desc: Stale cache, breadcrumbs that multiplied each build, a symlink into my own environment, and local-only images: four deploy incidents on Cloudflare Pages.

hosting-compare.title: Static hosting compared: Cloudflare, Netlify, Vercel
hosting-compare.desc: Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, Vercel, GitHub Pages and Firebase Hosting compared by official terms (Oct 2026): ads allowed, free limits, file limits, config.

comment-services.title: Comment systems compared: giscus, Disqus, Remark42
comment-services.desc: giscus, utterances, Disqus, Remark42, Cusdis, Staticman and Commento compared by official pages (Oct 2026): storage, ads and tracking, maintenance status.

ios-sdk-compare.title: iOS ad SDKs compared: AdMob, AppLovin, LevelPlay
ios-sdk-compare.desc: AdMob, AppLovin MAX, LevelPlay, Firebase and Supabase compared by official pages (Oct 2026): payouts, privacy manifests, minimum Xcode, free tiers.

claude-vs-gemini-api.title: Claude API vs Gemini API: official numbers compared
claude-vs-gemini-api.desc: Claude and Gemini API compared by official pages (Oct 2026): small-model prices, web search cost and caps, spend limits, deprecation notice.

gemini-migration.title: Claude to Gemini API migration: 16 calls, 1 function
gemini-migration.desc: Moving an iOS app backend from Claude Haiku 4.5 to Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite: choosing by deprecation date, one wrapper, a search cap breaker, a kill switch.

fail-open.title: Fail-open let resale items through: the fix
fail-open.desc: A gate that let items pass when the list price could not be confirmed had a blind spot: a daily search cap. Telling “did not know” from “could not look.”

blocked-page.title: A scraper read a notice page as success: 0 products
blocked-page.desc: A scraper returned zero products for three days because a 2,410-byte “enable JavaScript” page counted as success. How I centralized the check.

webaudio.title: Measuring WebAudio waveforms to set game volume
webaudio.desc: A browser game with no audio files: koto, taiko and gong synthesized with WebAudio. I could not listen, so I set volume by measuring waveform peaks.

ranking-free-tier.title: Halving Cloudflare D1 free-tier use: 5 calls to 2
ranking-free-tier.desc: A game ranking on Workers and D1: calls per play from 5 to 2, rows read from 421 to 221. Server-side rank counting and removing the preflight call.

torecadash-review.title: Four things before App Review: ITMS-91064 and more
torecadash-review.desc: Before submitting an iOS app, four things stopped me: iPad screenshots, ITMS-91064, account deletion (5.1.1(v)) and user-content reporting (1.2), and how I fixed each.

scrape-cost.title: Re-measuring scraper cost: 1/8 of the credits
scrape-cost.desc: I believed two sites could not be fetched more often because of cost. Comparing three Scrape.do settings showed rendering was wasted: 3x faster, 1/8 the credits.

bulk-accident.title: A bulk update hit all articles: count, then write
bulk-accident.desc: A bulk job hit every article and wrongly restored 18 items. How I reverted them from status history and proved new tests work by breaking rules one at a time.

dup-zero.title: I counted zero duplicates; the audit found 112 pairs
dup-zero.desc: A nightly merge job timed out partway through the first genre, so later genres were never reached. My count of zero saw only that genre. Fixed with a rotating budget.

torecadash-ai.title: Cutting AI calls: 45% became 4.5%, batching ran 0 times
torecadash-ai.desc: Reducing calls to an AI in a trading-card app: a predicted 45% cut was 4.5%, and batching ran zero times after deploy. What I found by recounting, with numbers.

stopwatch-rank.title: A fair 10-second stopwatch ranking: decimals and ties
stopwatch-rank.desc: Why I truncate to three decimals so coarse clocks get no advantage, how ties (a 1/333 chance) are broken, and how I counted KV writes on the free tier.

anime-db.title: 16,177 titles to 6,091: building an anime database
anime-db.desc: An anime quiz picks from about 6,000 titles. Where they came from, the criterion that cut 62.3% of 16,177, what remains, and the biases of the method.

match-percent.title: Quiz match % disagreed with the ranking: 35-40%
match-percent.desc: An anime quiz’s match percentage used a different yardstick from its ranking. With the old display, 35 to 40% of 1,000 synthetic respondents saw a reversed top 3.

shindan12.title: Anime quiz: 12 questions vs 50, how much changes
shindan12.desc: A 50-question anime quiz now gives a result after 12. Measured with 1,000 synthetic respondents: the type mostly matches, but the single recommended title changes a lot.

result-screen.title: Fixing an anime quiz result screen: 29% wrong links
result-screen.desc: The anime quiz showed the same two streaming buttons for every title; about 29% were wrong. How I narrowed buttons by availability and fixed image problems.

first-visit.title: Six buttons to one: a first-time player screen
first-visit.desc: A browser game title screen had six things to press. I made the first step one button, and fixed saves vanishing inside an iframe and play continuing in a hidden tab.

sushi-measure.title: “The pile settles at 89%” was wrong: a bad measurement
sushi-measure.desc: Rebalancing a merge puzzle, I found my measurement had counted falling pieces. Three causes: a backward size ladder, a pit-shaped tub, and pieces tunneling the floor.
